title: Good-truncation normalization and exact-functor compatibility
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary derived categories $D(\mathcal C),D(\mathcal D)$, localization functors $Q$, and cohomology functors $H^a$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $S_{\mathcal C}(B)=B[0]$ for the single-complex functor, and use good truncations [def-kun-truncations]. Let $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ be the full subcategory of objects $K$ with $H^a(K)=0$ for $a\ne0$; define $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal D}$ similarly.
For every representing complex $C^\bullet$ of $K\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$, let $c_C:\tau_{\le0}C\to C$ be the truncation inclusion and let $p_C:\tau_{\le0}C\to H^0(C)[0]$ have degree-zero component $\ker d_C^0\twoheadrightarrow\ker d_C^0/\operatorname{im}d_C^{-1}$ and zero components elsewhere. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and, under the canonical comparison $H^0(QC)\cong H^0(C)$, the formula
$$\epsilon_{QC}=Q(p_C)\circ Q(c_C)^{-1}$$
defines a representative-independent natural isomorphism $\epsilon_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathcal C}H^0(K)$ on $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$. In particular, for every derived morphism $a:K\to L$ in this subcategory,
$$\epsilon_L\circ a=S_{\mathcal C}(H^0(a))\circ\epsilon_K.$$
For $K,L\in\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$, $a\mapsto H^0(a)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(K,L)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(H^0(K),H^0(L))$; equivalently $H^0(a)$ is the unique $b$ with $S_{\mathcal C}(b)=\epsilon_La\epsilon_K^{-1}$.
Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and preserve finite limits and colimits, and let $D(F)$ be its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $\chi_{F,K}:FH^0(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(D(F)K)$ be induced by preservation of kernels, images and quotients, and let $\sigma_{F,B}:D(F)S_{\mathcal C}(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathcal D}(FB)$ be the termwise single-complex comparison. Then $D(F)$ sends $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal C}$ into $\mathcal Z_{\mathcal D}$ and
$$\epsilon_{D(F)K}=S_{\mathcal D}(\chi_{F,K})\circ\sigma_{F,H^0(K)}\circ D(F)(\epsilon_K),$$
$$H^0(D(F)a)\circ\chi_{F,K}=\chi_{F,L}\circ F(H^0(a)).$$
For identity functors these comparisons are identities under the canonical identification $D(\operatorname{id})\cong\operatorname{id}$; for two composable exact functors their comparisons are the composites of the individual comparisons under the canonical termwise derived-composition isomorphism. The assertions also hold in the zero abelian category.

proof.text: Identify the boundary term of the good truncation with cycles and its inclusion with iCycles, by dualizing the canonical truncGE projection formula. Monomorphism cancellation and the chain-map equation identify the incoming differential with the original differential factored through cycles. The homology quotient kills it, so the stipulated goodTruncationProjection is a chain map.

Use the existing uniquely H⁰-normalized degree-zero identification to define epsilon. Conjugate maps by these identifications and use full faithfulness of the single functor. H⁰ is faithful between single objects because the single-homology comparison identifies its composite with single with the identity. Thus H⁰ is injective between the concentrated objects. Its inverse on Hom sets is b mapped to epsilon_K followed by S(b) followed by epsilon_L inverse. The normalization equations and naturality of the single-homology comparison prove naturality and the unique-b characterization.

Compute H⁰ of the projection by precomposing with the epimorphism from cycles. Naturality of homologyπ and cycles inclusions, and the explicit degree-zero component, show that H⁰(p_A) followed by the single-homology comparison equals H⁰(c_A). Transfer this equality through the localization homology factorization. Vanishing transported along r makes A isLE 0, so c_A is a quasi-isomorphism. H⁰-injectivity from the preceding step identifies the specified roof equation with epsilon_K. All other factors in this equation are isomorphisms, so Q(p_A) is an isomorphism and p_A is a quasi-isomorphism.

For every degree n, use the canonical exact-functor homology comparison. Its source is zero when Hⁿ(K) is zero, because an additive functor preserves zero objects. Hence the derived image stays concentrated in degree zero. Naturality of this comparison is the second asserted exact-functor equation.

Apply H⁰-injectivity to the exact-functor normalization formula and postcompose with the single-homology comparison. Use naturality of chi on epsilon_K and compatibility of chi with the single comparison, already proved in the source library. The resulting composite is F(H⁰(epsilon_K) followed by the single-homology comparison) followed by chi_K, hence chi_K. Cancel chi_K to obtain the required formula. No separate construction of a functor-versus-truncation comparison is needed.

For the identity functor the short-complex homology comparison is identity by the canonical homology-map-data equation. The derived identity comparison evaluated at a complex is its localization factorization, by the homotopy-category identity equation. These computations prove the homology identity after precomposition with Q; localization faithfulness descends it. The single identity follows by evaluating the termwise single comparison.

For composition, compare the direct preserved homology data with iterated preservation. Their cycle isomorphisms agree by monomorphism cancellation and their homology isomorphisms by cancellation of the cycles quotient epimorphism. This proves the complex homology comparison composition equation. To descend it, compare the two natural transformations in the displayed derived equation after Q, cancel the factorization isomorphisms, and use naturality of chi and the canonical derived-composition factorization. Localization faithfulness gives the desired equality on every object. The source library single-comparison composition theorem proves the other conjunct. Every argument permits zero objects and zero categories.
